card.lives_in: Ossett, West Yorkshire (Yorkshire and The Humber)
card.occupation: Regional Operations Manager for a builders' merchants and timber supplies firm, responsible for six branches across West and South Yorkshire
card.education_detail: Left Ossett School after A-levels (Business Studies, Geography, General Studies), did a part-time HND in Business and Finance at Wakefield College while working as a branch admin clerk, and later completed a company-funded CMI Level 5 Certificate in Management and Leadership
card.household: Lives with her husband Gary (51), a self-employed electrician, in a four-bedroom detached house on a 2000s estate on the edge of Ossett. Their son Callum (22) has moved out to a flat in Leeds, and their daughter Megan (19) is at university in Nottingham and comes home for holidays. They have a black Labrador called Bella.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Wakefield in a working-class family. Her dad worked at a glassworks and her mum was a dinner lady. She was christened and confirmed Church of England and still calls herself Christian. In practice she goes to church for Christmas, weddings, funerals and the odd Remembrance Sunday. She is proud of having 'done well' compared with where she started, and she pays attention to the markers of that: the house, the car and holidays abroad. Her views are traditional and fairly settled.
card.professional_persona: She has been with the same firm for 24 years and worked up from admin clerk to branch manager to her current role. She is results-focused, commercially sharp and good at managing upwards. She likes the status of the job: the company Audi, the bonus, being the one who gets called when something goes wrong. She will quietly take credit for a branch's turnaround and is not above shading figures in her favour at a quarterly review. She sees that as 'just how it works'. She is fair enough with staff who keep their heads down but has little patience for 'moaners'. She sticks to the procedures the company already has rather than trying new systems.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself. She walks Bella most evenings and has a gym membership she uses in fits and starts, mostly in January. She watches the rugby league with Gary because he's a Wakefield Trinity fan, and she enjoys the corporate hospitality boxes more than the game itself. She follows Strictly-style celebrity sport stories rather than results.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest in galleries, theatre or 'arty' films. She watches crime dramas, Gogglebox, I'm a Celebrity and whatever is on Saturday night telly, and rewatches series she already knows she likes. She'll go to a musical in Leeds or Bradford if it's a well-known one and makes a nice night out with dinner beforehand. She reads holiday paperbacks and listens to Heart or Greatest Hits Radio in the car.
card.travel_persona: Likes reliable, comfortable holidays rather than exploring. She has been to the same four-star all-inclusive in Tenerife several times, plus Majorca and Turkey with the kids when they were younger. She and Gary have started doing a 'nice' city break once a year, last time Dubai, which she chose partly so she could post about it. She likes a long weekend in Whitby or a lodge with a hot tub in the Dales. She isn't interested in backpacking or anywhere she'd 'have to rough it'.
card.culinary_persona: She cooks a solid weekday repertoire: spaghetti bolognese, chilli, chicken fajitas, a roast on Sunday with proper Yorkshire puddings. She calls the evening meal 'tea'. She doesn't like unfamiliar food and will pick the steak or chicken on most menus. She likes going out for a meal at 'nice' places in Harrogate or Leeds, especially somewhere a bit fancy that she can mention at work, and she enjoys a prosecco or a gin and tonic at the weekend.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog round the local park and canal path
watching crime dramas and reality TV
meals out and the occasional spa day with friends
keeping the house and garden looking smart
shopping for clothes and handbags at the Trinity Walk and White Rose centres
skills: negotiating with suppliers and trade customers
Excel and the company's stock system
presenting figures to senior management in a favourable light
card.career_goals: To move up to Operations Director before she's 55, partly for the money and title, and partly because she thinks she's been overlooked once already. She'd like to retire comfortably at around 60 with a good pension, and maybe buy a holiday apartment in Spain.
card.voice: A clear West Yorkshire accent, toned down slightly into a more polished 'work voice' on calls. She speaks at a brisk, confident pace and gets to the point. She uses 'erm' when she's thinking, and 'sort of' and 'you know' fairly often. She says 'tea' for the evening meal, and phrases like 'I were knackered' slip out when she relaxes. She's polite, with plenty of 'thanks' and 'sorry, can you say that again?', but if she gets a question she thinks is pointless she can sound a bit impatient. She doesn't like silence and will fill it with a quick 'so, yeah, that's about it really' or ask whether you need anything else.
card.typing: Types quickly and mostly correctly. She uses capitals at the start of sentences and full stops, and she gets apostrophes right because she 'can't stand' bad spelling in work emails. Answers are short and practical, sometimes just a phrase. She occasionally uses 'etc' or '&', and she doesn't use emojis or text-speak in a form.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, assured and businesslike. She's quick to mention her job title and that she manages several sites. She comes across as capable and a bit pleased with herself, but chatty enough to be good company. She tends to steer conversation towards practical topics and her own experiences, and gives short answers to anything abstract or 'airy-fairy'.
small_things: Bella the Labrador needing walking whatever the weather
the traffic on the M1 or around Junction 40
Gary being out on jobs till all hours
getting her nails done before a work do
the price of everything going up
a new handbag she treated herself to
deeper_things: She feels she was passed over for a director role a few years ago in favour of a younger man and still resents it
She worries the kids don't need her much any more and the house feels quiet
Her dad's health is declining and she feels guilty she doesn't visit Wakefield as often as her sister does
She sometimes stretches expenses or bends the rules at work and thinks everyone does, but wouldn't want it said out loud
She's privately anxious about getting older and 'letting herself go'
She and Gary have rows about money because she likes to spend and he's more cautious
card.webcam_photo: A head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam slightly below eye level, angled a little upward. Soft daylight comes in from a window to her left, with a ceiling light on as well, giving even, slightly warm lighting. She is a white woman in her late forties with a fair complexion, light makeup, defined eyebrows and a neat, confident smile, looking straight at the camera. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted blonde with darker roots, blow-dried and tucked behind one ear. She wears a fitted navy blouse with small gold stud earrings and a thin gold necklace, and no glasses. Behind her is a spare bedroom used as a home office, with pale grey painted walls. A white floating shelf holds a framed photo of two young adults at a graduation, a small potted artificial succulent and a scented candle. A tall grey wardrobe is partly visible on the right, and the edge of a canvas print reading 'Home' in silver lettering shows at the top left.
